description.narrative:
Oxfam/Somalia/land is implementing a programme in Somalia with the goal of amplifying and supporting the voices of the most vulnerable groups and their capacity within the context of the climate emergency. The strategic objective of the AACJ programme isto mobilize citizens, companies, and governments to advance climate justice, specifically contributing to: 1. Amplified voices of people who are disproportionately affected by the changing climate, offering solutions for a more sustainable future, such as women, youth, andlocal and indigenous communities. 2. African narratives that highlight lived experiences of women, youth, and local and indigenous communities impacted by climate change, helping to change the terms of the debate on climate change. 3. Policy and practice changes that prevent adverse impacts of climate change, support communities already affected, and enable the transition to more sustainable,low-carbon economies, leaving no one behind.
Objectives. • Identify and showcase climateaction initiatives across Somalia/land, especially those led by women, marginalized groups, and youth. - Produce and distribute a film/documentary showcasing these stories with Somali language narration and English subtitles or dubbing. • Facilitate anddevelop an open, transparent mechanism for selecting social influencers /Climate activist who will contribute to climate action in Somalia. • Facilitate public debates on climate justice topics, including economic development in the context of climatechange.
Scope of Work Some of the indicative activities include the following, however, the CSO /CBOs will propose the activities based on the local contexts. • Identifying Inspiring Stories/Initiatives: Document inspiring climate action initiatives, focusing on those led by women, marginalized groups, and youth. Engage with local communities for diverse representation. • Facilitating Climate Action Social Influencers: Establish a transparent mechanism to select climate action influencers and supporttheir initiatives. • Organizing Public Debates on Climate Justice: Collaborate with think tanks and experts to organize debates on climate justice, focusing on economic growth under climate change.
Deliverables • Documentary or short film with Englishsubtitles or dubbing inspiring climate action initiatives, focusing on those led by women, marginalized groups, and youth. Engage with local communities for diverse representation. • Detailed criteria (Transparent mechanism) for selecting climate actioninfluencers. • Documented Series of public debates on climate justice. • One final financial and Narrative report.
Expected Outputs • 2 types of connections/events reuniting civil society organizations and networks. • 2 types of climate justice narratives developed and spread. • 85 people involved in actions, disaggregated by gender, age, disability, and indigenous status.
Expected Outcomes • Stronger connections among movements of women, youth, and indigenous communities. • Documented andadopted locally shaped climate solutions. • Amplified voices of grassroots communities. • Enhanced capacity of local communities on climate change topics.

participating-org.narrative: WASDA was established as a nongovernmental in Somalia in 2001. The organisation strives to supplement the efforts of governments and other development stakeholders in addressing developmental challenges in the Horn of Africa. WASDA is currently implementing development initiatives in North-Eastern Kenya and parts of Southern Somalia. WASDA has been working with pastoral communities in North-Eastern Kenya and Southern Somalia for 23 years. The organisation has, in the process, gained and built a wealth of experience and knowledge that informs its programming. It utilises limited resources to change the lives of millions of people in its geographical areas of operation. In the last 23 years, WASDA has reached over 1.5 million people with livelihood, food security; water; sanitation and hygiene; health and nutrition; education and emergency humanitarian support. VISION Empowered communities in the Horn of Africa that are resilient, innovative and peaceful MISSION To mobilize and engage communities and other stakeholders in creating strategic partnerships for sustainable management of the environment, water resources, livelihoods, and education and public health services in the Horn of Africa.
